scope: Python (Everglades). Question: where are Burmese pythons active and where should removal crews go next? Burmese python only, in the South Florida Everglades region (bbox -83.2, 24.3, -79.8, 27.5). Other species (tegu, iguana, lionfish, carp) and places outside the region are refused with this scope. The hotspot score is a labelled heuristic, not a probability or population estimate.

newTools.name: weather_forecast
newTools.purpose: NWS gridpoint forecast periods for a site or point (api.weather.gov), with the office updateTime used for freshness.
newTools.input: { site?: string (carp location id or name), lat?: number, lon?: number, periods?: number (default 6) }
newTools.output: { office, grid, updateTime, periods: [{ name, start, end, temperatureF, windSpeed, windDirection, precipProbability, shortForecast }] }

newTools.name: source_info
newTools.purpose: Static facts about one feed of the active app: publisher, API URL, human page, licence and attribution text, cadence, typical latency, rate limit, coverage limits, and what the feed can and cannot tell us. Read from the app config, no network call.
newTools.input: { feed: string (a feed id of the active app, e.g. usgs, nwps, crw) } or {} for all feeds
newTools.output: rows of { feed, publisher, apiUrl, pageUrl, licence, attribution, cadence, latency, rateLimit, coverage, limits[] }

newTools.name: evidence
newTools.purpose: Fetch one cited record by evidence id (wraps GraphQL `evidence(id)`): the record, its source API URL, publisher page, fetch time, ingest lag, feed state and links such as duplicateOf or the forecast issuance it belongs to.
newTools.input: { id: string (C14 evidence id, e.g. reading:..., sighting:..., forecast:...) }
newTools.output: { id, kind, record, sourceUrl, sourcePageUrl, fetchedAt, ingestLagSeconds, feed, links[] }

newTools.name: team_board
newTools.purpose: Read the active app's team board (GraphQL `board(id: "<app>:main")`): missions with their sites or areas and dates, and committed messages with author, recipient, thread and time. Human records, not a data feed.
newTools.input: { kind?: 'missions' | 'messages' | 'all', about?: string (place, site or area name), hours?: number (default 168) }
newTools.output: { missions: [{ id, title, place, bbox, start, end, assignees }], messages: [{ id, from, to, thread, at, body }] }

changelog.change: python-explain-cold-snap-drop, python-replay-cold-snap-map, python-replay-scores-during-cold: the cold snap is January 2026 (the fixture reference time is 2026-01-15T03:00Z with a Cold Weather Advisory from 2026-01-14T22:00Z; February 2026 is after the reference time, so no data could exist for it). Question text and view hints changed from February to January; pass criteria unchanged.
python-replay-cold-snap-map: pass phrase (February|2026-02) follows the January rename: (January|2026-01).
python-replay-scores-during-cold: the change phrase accepted five verbs; "declined", "lower", "unchanged" and the like describe the same movement, so the pattern now takes them (1 pattern).
python-replay-30d: the span phrase accepted only "30 days"; "30-day replay" names the same span, so the pattern now takes either spelling (1 pattern).

J1 (gates/leaf-J1.md): pass.phrases (regexes) migrated to pass.mustSay: every regex phrase became a plain-language statement judged by an independent model (apps/web/eval/judge.ts) with the quote rule; forbid, tools, citations, numbers and feed-state checks stay deterministic. Script: scripts/migrate-phrases-to-mustsay.ts.

J1 wording review after the first live run: statements that read as conjunctions or carried the intent rather than the regex were reworded to the regex's meaning after the first live run (docs/grading/judge-validation.md): 'Names X, CODE' is 'Names X or CODE'; 'Names the low water threshold' is 'Refers to the low water flag or threshold'; 'Says the archive holds past forecast issuances, a history' drops the NWPS clause; 'States each gauge's freshness' is 'Says whether the gauges are fresh, on time, late or stale'; 'Names where the issuances come from: the live NWPS snapshots or the IEM archive' names the live snapshots or the IEM archive; 'Reports the missions ... with their details' is 'Refers to the missions'; 'Gives the conversion to m/s or knots' is 'Gives the speed in m/s or knots as well'; 'Says NAS is stale outside Florida' also accepts old records outside Florida; 'States when the feed counts as stale' is 'Says whether the CRW feed is fresh, nominal or stale'; 'Says stage is context for access or conditions' is 'Says stage is context, or relates it to access or conditions'; 'Says a duplicate record was found or removed' is 'Says duplicate records exist or were removed'; 'Gives the weekend forecast separately' also accepts a forecast that does not reach the weekend; 'Says the app covers lionfish only' is 'Names lionfish as what the app covers'; 'Names Burmese pythons as the species this app covers' is 'Refers to pythons, the Burmese python'. Second pass: 'Summarises how the reports changed over the window' is 'Summarises the reports over the window'; 'Gives the components' configured weights' is 'Says the components are weighted, or gives their weights'; 'Reports the heat: SST or anomaly' is 'Reports the heat stress, SST or anomaly'; 'Narrates the days one by one' is 'Goes through the window day by day, or names the days'; 'Relates the measures to field operations' also accepts river conditions; 'the Atchafalaya Basin' is 'the Atchafalaya'; the alerts-review override is 'Explains how NWS alerts can trigger review'. Third pass, after the second live run: every remaining 'each site's', 'per site', 'with its …' or semicolon clause that the regex did not require was dropped or turned into an 'or' (26 statements), for example 'Names the sites that need review' for the regex 'review' is 'Refers to the review status or which sites need review', 'States the forecast error per site' is 'States the forecast error or difference'. No statement was loosened below its regex.

cold-night caveat questions: the forbid 'pythons (will|won't|will not) (be )?(move|active|out)' matched the required limit 'the data cannot say whether pythons will be active'; it now ignores a negation word earlier in the sentence (whether/if/that/say/tell/know/show), as the carp safety forbids do. 1 pattern(s).
